title: The Mor functor from a finite free affine scheme into an affine scheme is representable by an affine scheme

standard_prerequisites.name: Explicit prerequisite boundary
standard_prerequisites.reference: The Mor functor, finite free modules, presentations of algebras, Yoneda; no cited result replaces the retained argument
standard_prerequisites.use: The functor Mor_S(Z,X) of S-morphisms, finite free modules and bases, presentations Gamma(X,O_X) = R[x_i]/(f_k), the Yoneda lemma, and pushforward/pullback of algebras along T -> S. The representing-object construction is retained in full.

core_obligations: Construct P = R[{a_{ij}}] and the ideal J generated by the coefficients c_{kj} of Psi(f_k), and show that W = Spec(P/J) is an S-scheme receiving a universal morphism b_univ : W x_S Z -> W x_S X.
Show b_univ induces a bijection W(T) -> Mor_S(Z,X)(T) for every affine T over S, using that b^sharp(1 tensor x_i) = sum alpha_{ij} tensor e_j is uniquely determined by the alpha_{ij}.

proof_roadmap.step: Choose the basis of Gamma(Z,O_Z) over R and a presentation of Gamma(X,O_X), define P and the R-algebra map Psi sending x_i to sum_j a_{ij} tensor e_j, and cut out J by the coefficients of the Psi(f_k).

spans.label: construction of P, Psi and J

proof_roadmap.step: Produce the universal morphism b_univ from the factorisation of Psi, and verify that W(T) -> Mor_S(Z,X)(T) is a bijection for affine T by solving for the alpha_{ij}.

spans.label: universal morphism and bijection on affine test schemes

difficulty_reason: Representability is proved by exhibiting the representing object explicitly and then checking the universal property on affine test schemes. The construction picks a finite basis e_1,...,e_m of Gamma(Z,O_Z) over R, a presentation of Gamma(X,O_X) by generators and relations, adjoins one variable a_{ij} per generator-and-basis-index pair, pushes the relations f_k through the resulting map Psi, and cuts out by the ideal J generated by all coefficients c_{kj} of Psi(f_k) along the basis. The load-bearing points are that the universal map b_univ factors through Gamma(X,O_X) and that the induced map W(T) -> Mor_S(Z,X)(T) is a bijection on affine T, which is where the finite-freeness of Gamma(Z,O_Z) over R is used. Retained author proof at lines 20107-20168.
